title: About Wheel of Names: How a Winner Is Drawn
description: Who runs Wheel of Names, how the wheel picks a winner inside your browser, and what it leaves out on purpose.
heroText: Wheel of Names turns a pasted list into a spinning wheel that picks one name with crypto.getRandomValues. It is for teachers calling on a student, hosts running a giveaway, and anyone who wants a fair draw instead of a decision made by hand.

ctas.label: Open the wheel and paste a list
See how the draw stays random

sections.title: Who runs this site
sections.body: Wheel of Names is an independent site run by its owner. There is no company behind it, no staff list and no invented founder story: one person builds the wheel, writes the pages and reads every message sent through the contact form. It is not affiliated with any other wheel site, classroom platform or brand named on these pages.

sections.title: How a result is made
sections.body: The whole draw happens on your own device, inside the browser tab you have open.

steps.title: It reads your list and weights
steps.body: The text you paste and the weight you set for each entry, from 1 to 10.

steps.title: It runs in the browser
steps.body: No entry text is sent to a server, so the tool keeps working offline once the page has loaded.

steps.title: It returns a result
steps.body: One winner drawn with crypto.getRandomValues, its chance of winning, and how many entries are left. A [raffle draw](/raffle-wheel/) returns several winners in order, and a [fairness test](/fairness/) reports each entry's observed count against its expected share.

sections.title: Where it runs, and what that limits
sections.body: The browser is what keeps lists private, and it also sets the tool's edges.

steps.title: A current browser
steps.body: Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari in a recent version. Very old browsers may lack the random source the draw relies on.

steps.title: A page that has loaded
steps.body: Spin on a page you have already opened. A hard refresh starts again with an empty list.

steps.title: A tab with room to work
steps.body: A few thousand entries and a 10,000-draw test both stay light. A tab already holding dozens of heavy pages may run slowly.

steps.title: No app install
steps.body: Offline use means the loaded page keeps spinning without a connection. There is nothing to download first.

sections.title: What it does not do
sections.body: Some features are absent by choice, not by accident.

steps.title: No sign-in to draw
steps.body: A paid plan exists for saved wheels and longer records, not to unlock the basic draw.

steps.title: No pictures
steps.body: Entries stay text and a weight: avatars are not accepted. A list comes in by pasting it, or by importing a .json or .txt file from Results & sharing.

steps.title: No check on who a name is
steps.body: The wheel picks from the list it is given and does not confirm that a name belongs to a real person.

steps.title: No entry handling
steps.body: It draws winners. Selling tickets, collecting entries and confirming prizes are for the host to do outside the wheel.

sections.title: Plans, briefly
sections.body: Free use covers spinning with the features the home page lists, and the [pricing page](/pricing/) states what the paid plans add. The numbers stay on that page so this one does not repeat them.
